explanation: Bucket citation counts, capping values above the paper count at n. Scan possible h values downward while accumulating papers with at least h citations. The first feasible h is maximal.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Histogram variants fill and scan n+1 buckets; sort variants pay sorting cost then scan once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. Histogram variants store n+1 counters; sorting/copy workspace is stated separately.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: While scanning h downward, papers counts exactly the entries whose capped citation count is at least h. Capping at n cannot change any feasible h≤n. The first h with papers≥h is feasible, and every larger h has already failed, so it is maximal.
walkthrough: For citations [0,2,4,7], there are only two papers with at least 3 citations, so h=3 fails. Three papers have at least 2 citations, so the answer is 2.
edgeCases: An empty list or all-zero citations gives zero.
Citation counts above the number of papers may be capped at n.
The number of qualifying papers can exceed h; equality is not required.
